description: Team omnitri-X| Working on NASA's "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. We use NASA satellite data, AI, and web tech to build smart solutions for agriculture, soil health, and water management. Open for software, UI/UX, and data science enthusiasts!
summary:
1. Smart Crop Rotation and Planting Planning
Analyzes past crop and growth data to protect soil fertility and optimize nitrogen balance.

Tells the farmer which crop to plant in the field next season to get the highest yield.

2. Drought and Agricultural Frost Early Warning
Continuously monitors the microclimate of the region where the field is located to detect sudden temperature drops (agricultural frost hazard) days in advance.

Reports drought stress caused by precipitation irregularities in advance, allowing farmers to take timely precautions.

3. Satellite-Assisted Field Health and NDVI Tracking
Regularly monitors the green canopy and plant growth health of the field through satellite imagery.

Pinpoints problem areas experiencing water stress, slowed growth, or disease on color-coded maps.

4. Water Footprint and Smart Irrigation Optimization
Calculates the actual water needs of the plant for that period to prevent wasteful flood irrigation.

Helps protect regional water resources while lowering the hidden water footprint of the field.

5. Natural Language Guidance and Decision Support
Allows farmers to converse directly with the system instead of having to review complex charts or reports.

Provides direct, clear, and understandable answers to questions such as "Do I need to irrigate the field this week?" or "Is there a frost risk in the coming days?"

Project Details: Tarla Asistanı

Tarla Asistanı is an AI-powered agricultural decision support and data analytics platform developed to safeguard agricultural production against the climate crisis, empower farmers to make informed decisions, and optimize resource management.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

  • What it does: Tarla Asistanı plans smart crop rotations, forecasts drought and agricultural frost risks days in advance, monitors field plant health (NDVI) via satellite imagery, and calculates optimal irrigation timing.
  • How it works: The system processes international open-source satellite data, geographic information systems, and meteorological data in the background. By integrating these technical insights through the Google Gemini API, it presents them in simple, everyday language via a direct chat interface. Instead of dealing with complex charts, farmers can simply ask questions like "Is there a frost risk this week?" or "Do I need to irrigate the field?" and receive clear, direct answers.(For example, you can test the system with the field located in Diyarbakır, Çınar, Aşağı Konak, Plot No: 101, Parcel No: 1).

2. What are its benefits?

  • Yield Increase: Recommends the most accurate crop rotation based on historical soil performance, boosting crop quality and quantity.
  • Cost and Resource Savings: Prevents wasteful flood irrigation, eliminating water waste and reducing the hidden water footprint.
  • Risk Management: Detects sudden temperature drops (agricultural frost) and drought stress early to prevent harvest losses.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to build a bridge between traditional farming methods and modern data science. By ensuring that small and medium-scale farmers can easily access advanced satellite data and AI analytics, we aim to contribute to food security, promote climate-resilient sustainable agricultural practices, and foster a culture of conscious production in local agriculture.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Technologies: Python, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, FastAPI, NumPy, and Pandas.
  • Data & API Sources: NASA POWER API, CropGraph API, Open-Meteo API, and NDVI satellite time series.
  • Visualization & Interface: Streamlit and Folium libraries (for interactive map and dashboard panels).
  • Hardware: High-performance laptops and cloud-based development environments.

5. How is your project creative?

Tarla Asistanı stands out by transforming technical and complex satellite/meteorological data into an easy-to-use natural language chat assistant. While most agricultural software bombards farmers with hard-to-read maps and graphs, our project allows them to communicate directly as if consulting an expert. Furthermore, its hybrid structure—combining NASA satellite data with regional microclimate forecasting—makes the project truly unique.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Usability (UX): Considering the digital literacy levels of farmers and agricultural workers, we ensured the interface was kept as simple, fast, and mobile-friendly as possible.
  • Accessibility and Cost: By choosing sustainable and open-source APIs, we made the system cost-effective, scalable, and adaptable to any region.
  • Local Needs: We prioritized the most critical risks brought by the climate crisis to regional agriculture, such as drought and sudden frost.
